Looking at this question, I need to identify which rRNA modification enzyme promotes large ribosomal subunit (50S) assembly even as a catalytically dead mutant, indicating a structural/scaffolding role beyond its enzymatic function.

Among the options:
- RluC, RlmN, RlmM, and RlmB are all rRNA modification enzymes involved in 23S rRNA processing.

Research on E. coli ribosome assembly has demonstrated that **RlmB** (a 2'-O-methyltransferase of 23S rRNA) plays a role in large subunit assembly that extends beyond its catalytic methyltransferase activity. When expressed as a catalytically dead mutant (unable to perform the actual 2'-O-methylation), RlmB still promotes 50S large ribosomal subunit assembly, indicating it has a structural/scaffolding function during the assembly pathway.

[ANSWER]E[/ANSWER]
